izzyondroid:inc.flide.vi8.name: 8Vim Keyboard
izzyondroid:inc.flide.vi8.summary: A small screen keyboard inspired by VIM and 8Pen
izzyondroid:inc.flide.vi8.description:
VI8 started essentially as a clone for 8pen, which for some reason they have stopped distributing.
 From the original 8vim description: „The 8vim draws inspiration from handwriting. By mimicking the way our hand moves when constrained to a square canvas, we are able to create a natural and fun writing experience, akin to doodling on a piece of paper. The layout is optimised for fast writing, by allowing for the most common letter sequences to be produced with swift, fluid gestures. Once familiar with the layout, you can reach speeds of 40 words per minute.“
 With 8pen you could actually type blind. Together with any text editor, you could get the job done, but you have to keep your both hands engaged and keep tapping on the various toolbars and buttons... I was missing VIM .
 I wanted my keyboard to also act as the editor. So VI8 , the Editor-in-Keyboard, was born. And here it is – try it out! And head over to the project page for more details.
 Usability Guide 
 So, what capabilities does 8Vim have? Once you know how to type with this thing (Learn how to type with this original 8Pen-game video ), you must know the following:
 Basic Needed Stuff: 
 Right Sector acts as a backspace Key.
 Bottom Sector acts as a Enter Key.
 Top Sector acts as a combination of SHIFT and CAPS_LOCK Key, i.e, Press once Shift is active, Press Twice CAPS is active and Press once more and everything is back to usual.
 Left Sector acts as the button that takes you to the Number Pad.
 Cursor Movements: 
 If you move your finger from the centre-circle to any sector and stay, the cursor movement will be emulated. For example, if you swipe from circle->right, the cursor will move right. You get the picture.
 Selection: 
 There is selection built in to the keyboard. if you move your finger from the right sector to the circle, the cursor will start moving left and selecting everything in it's path. once you release, a selection keyboard will open up for various stupidities to do.
 Paste Functionality: 
 Moving your finger from right->circle->lift-your-finger performs a paste. whatever is in the clipboard.

fdroid:com.florianthaler.githo.name: Githo
fdroid:com.florianthaler.githo.description:
G et I nto T he H abit O f…
Acquiring habits that stick can be difficult. Githo helps you by letting you gradually advance, instead of going from 0 to 100%.
This principle borrows ideas from exposure therapy.
Define levels of your final habit, going from easy to hard. Then start with the first one. Level up by consistently succeeding. If a level is too difficult (= if success isn't consistent), repeat the previous one.
Such a gradual acquisition reduces the physical/mental strain and helps you create a routine long before arriving at the final habit .
 Example of a Habit-Plan: 
Final Habit: Go jogging every morning 
Levels: Every morning... 
 * Week 1: Just step outside on the street, then return home.
 * Week 2: Take a walk around your house/building.
 * Week 3: Take a walk spanning 3-5 buildings.
 * Week 4: Take a longer walk and add short jogging-segments into the mix.
 * Week 5: Go jogging. Well done.
 Permissions 
Permissions are only used to display notifications.

fdroid:com.github.bmx666.appcachecleaner.name: Cache Cleaner
fdroid:com.github.bmx666.appcachecleaner.summary: Clean cache of installed user and system apps using Accessibility
fdroid:com.github.bmx666.appcachecleaner.description:
Since the release of Android 6 (Marshmallow), the option to clear the cache of all apps at once has been restricted by Google to system apps only. This means that users no longer have the convenience of clearing the cache of all their apps simultaneously. To clear the cache of individual apps, one must manually navigate to each app's "App Info" screen, locate the "Storage" menu, and then select the "Clean cache" button.
To simplify this process and save time, Cache Cleaner requests a list of installed apps on your device and utilizes the Accessibility service to replace the manual steps involved in clearing the cache. This allows for a more convenient and automated process of cache cleaning.
 Cache Cleaner provides the added benefit of customizable app lists. This functionality allows you to create personalized lists of specific apps, giving you the flexibility to selectively clear the cache of only the apps you choose.

fdroid:com.nooto.app.summary: Cross-platform, privacy-focused notes with end-to-end encryption
fdroid:com.nooto.app.description:
Nooto is a note-taking app that keeps your notes private. Everything is encrypted on your device before it ever leaves it, using AES-256-GCM encryption with keys derived locally via Argon2id. Nobody but you, not even the server operator, can read your notes.
 Features: 
 Notes are encrypted on-device before sync; the server only ever sees ciphertext
 Works fully offline, no account required to use the app locally
 Optional sync across devices, using the built-in public server or your own self-hosted instance
 Folders, drag-and-drop organization, and a markdown editor
 Fully open source and auditable
 What the server stores: only an opaque note ID and ciphertext blobs for content and metadata. No readable title, no readable content, no plaintext of any kind.
 Please note: Nooto is beta software and still under active development. The encryption design has not yet been reviewed by an independent security auditor. Use at your own discretion, and please report issues on the project's GitHub page.

Log drinks from a curated catalog, watch your active caffeine level in real time on a 24-hour curve, and get a personalized sleep forecast based on your unique metabolism.

• Real-time 24-hour caffeine curve with emoji drink markers
• Personalized pharmacokinetic modeling based on age, weight, lifestyle
• Sleep forecast — see if caffeine will affect your bedtime
• Curated drink catalog: coffee, tea, energy drinks, soda
• Barcode scanning, live or from a photo, with an optional Open Food Facts lookup
• Typo-tolerant drink search and tea re-steep tracking
• Drink detail sheets showing individual contribution curves
• Quick actions — edit, duplicate, or delete entries
• Analytics: caffeine by source, bedtime impact, and when you drink it, hour by hour

• Montserrat typography and haptic feedback throughout
• Full dark mode support
 Privacy:

• The internet is only used if you choose to look up a scanned barcode on Open Food Facts, and only the barcode number is sent
• No ads, no tracking, no telemetry, no accounts
• Open source (GPL-3.0)
 Science:

fdroid:dev.khoj.pitaka.fdroid.name: Pitak
fdroid:dev.khoj.pitaka.fdroid.summary: Privacy-first offline library catalogue with an encrypted lending vault
fdroid:dev.khoj.pitaka.fdroid.description:
Pitak is a privacy-first, offline personal library catalogue. Catalogue your books, lend them to borrowers from an encrypted vault, keep a wishlist, import/export your data, make portable backups, and optionally publish a read-only library site.
Features:
* Library — add, edit, search, sort and filter books; soft-delete with restore; on-device cover capture; ISBN barcode scan with metadata lookup (Open Library → Google Books, chained and cached).
* Borrowers vault — a persistent, AES-256-GCM encrypted store for borrowers and loans, unlocked by a passphrase (Argon2id key derivation). Optional biometric unlock.
* Wishlist — track books to acquire; move them to the library on purchase.
* Import / Export — JSON, CSV (including Goodreads import), and paginated PDF export with Indic-script support.
* Backup / Restore — portable .pitabak archives.
* Publish — optionally push a read-only library viewer to GitHub Pages, with PII redaction.
* Library network — save other Pitak libraries and browse their published catalogues inside the app (search, filter, sort, read-only detail), with an explicit "Open in browser" fallback.
* App-lock — optional biometric/device-credential gate before the library screen.
Privacy posture: local-first by default. Sensitive data lives in the platform Keystore; secrets are held as wipeable bytes. Network calls happen only on explicit user action (ISBN lookup, publish, Refresh, opening a saved library, opt-in remote covers). A catalogue you open is not stored on your device, and its cover images load only while you view it and only if the remote-cover switch is on. Screenshots are blocked while sensitive data is visible.
The cryptographic core is written in Rust and built entirely from source.

fdroid:es.manifold.sidedeck.name: SideDeck
fdroid:es.manifold.sidedeck.summary: Free DJ app. Mix on your phone. No subscriptions.
fdroid:es.manifold.sidedeck.description:
SideDeck is a free, open-source DJ app for Android. Mix local files on dual decks, or plug in a USB mixer such as the Teenage Engineering EP-136 K.O. Sidekick and mix on the hardware. No monthly subscription, no paywall, no premium tier.
MIX ON THE PHONE, OR ON HARDWARE
Use SideDeck as a standalone DJ app: landscape dual decks, waveforms, 3-band EQ, filter, and a crossfader. Or connect a USB mixer and send Deck A and Deck B out as separate stereo channels so you EQ, cue, and mix on the device.
SideDeck is built to work with the Teenage Engineering EP-136 K.O. Sidekick. Connect the EP-136 over USB, set Sidekick USB mode to Multi, and enable the external mixer in SideDeck. Deck A and Deck B go out separately so you can mix on the EP-136. The on-screen EQ and crossfader step aside so you're mixing on the hardware, not fighting a software mixer.
Other USB mixers that can take Deck A and Deck B as separate outputs work the same way.
YOUR MUSIC, YOUR SERVER
SideDeck plays tracks from your phone and from a Subsonic music server. Point it at any Subsonic-compatible library, browse albums and tracks, and download them to the device.
Load music from folders on the phone. Analyze BPM and musical key on load. The library highlights keys that sit well with what's already on a deck.
WHAT YOU CAN DO
• Dual-deck landscape DJ layout with waveforms
• Sync, loops, BPM nudge and jump
• Internal mixer: 3-band EQ, filter, crossfader
• USB out to the Teenage Engineering EP-136 K.O. Sidekick (and similar mixers)
• Subsonic browse and download
• Local library with BPM and key analysis
FREE AND OPEN SOURCE
SideDeck is GNU GPL v3 software. There is no subscription, no in-app DJ "pro" unlock. If you want a DJ app that works with the Teenage Engineering EP-136 K.O. Sidekick, talks to a Subsonic server, and stays free, this is it.
Requires Android 8.0 or later. USB host (OTG) on the phone if you use an external mixer such as the EP-136 K.O. Sidekick.

fdroid:io.github.buerlino.gridload.name: GridLoad
fdroid:io.github.buerlino.gridload.summary: Shows when to run your appliances, based on the dynamic electricity price
fdroid:io.github.buerlino.gridload.description:
GridLoad tells you at a glance whether now is a good time to run household appliances like the washing machine, dishwasher or EV charger. It reads your tariff's dynamic electricity price, or the day-ahead market price, and shows one colour:
 Green, good time: electricity is cheap, run your appliances now.
 Orange, fair time: average price, only run what you need.
 Red, bad time: electricity is expensive, wait if you can.
The price now is compared with the next 24 hours, so red means a cheaper time is coming, and the app shows when the next good time starts. A price curve shows those prices in their colours and how long the green lasts. Cheap times are when the grid has the most to spare, for example at midday when solar power peaks. Shifting load to those times lowers your bill and helps the grid.
 Regions: in Switzerland the price comes from your local utility's dynamic tariff: Central Switzerland (CKW), Canton of Zurich (EKZ), Einsiedeln (EKZ Einsiedeln), Fribourg and Neuchâtel (Groupe E), Northwestern Switzerland (Primeo Energie), Olten area (AVAG) and Gretzenbach (ELAG). In Austria, Belgium (Flanders, and Wallonia and Brussels), Germany, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg and the Netherlands it's the day-ahead market price (Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de, via energy-charts.info, CC BY 4.0); enter your supplier's add-on to see your own price. On a fixed-price tariff the colour doesn't change your bill, but it still shows when the grid has power to spare.
 whatwatt: with a whatwatt Go smart meter reader on your home Wi-Fi (with its Plus licence, wherever its adapter fits your meter), GridLoad also shows what your home draws right now and what that costs per hour.
 Peak load: some tariffs also charge for the month's highest 15-minute average (for example CKW's Home dynamic, Flanders, and Austria from 2027). With a whatwatt, GridLoad shows this quarter hour's projected draw against a limit (by default the month's highest, raised to what your biggest appliance needs and the least your tariff bills; each part, and a goal of your own, can be switched on or off) and how many kW are still free, and warns with a red bar and a vibration when it reaches the limit, with a Share button to tell your household. A history shows each day's highest quarter hour this month; tap it for a day's quarter hours and last month. Below it, your base load: what your home always draws, and what it comes to in a year. A small recorder script that GridLoad installs on the whatwatt saves every quarter hour on its SD card, also while the app is closed, and the app tells you exactly when it stops.
 Appliances: measure each appliance once with the whatwatt, and GridLoad says per appliance whether to switch it on now or wait, and until when: so it doesn't reach the limit, or, for a dishwasher or washing machine, because a later start is clearly cheaper. A waiting row sets a timer for the later start and says what waiting saves.
 Privacy: no account, no ads, no tracking. Internet access loads today's and tomorrow's prices from the utility or Energy-Charts. On Android 17 and later, the local network permission lets the app read your whatwatt; it's asked for only if you connect one.

fdroid:net.af0.where.description:
Where is a cross-platform, end-to-end encrypted realtime location sharing app.
Where is designed so the server learns as little as possible:
* No accounts. Identity is a device-scoped ephemeral key pair — no usernames, email addresses, or persistent IDs.
* End-to-end encrypted by default. Location payloads are encrypted with a Double Ratchet protocol before they leave the device. The server routes opaque ciphertext and cannot read coordinates.
* No social graph. Routing uses pairwise anonymous tokens; the server cannot reconstruct who is sharing with whom.
* Forward secrecy. Automated keepalives advance the ratchet even when only one party is sharing, so past sessions cannot be decrypted if a key is later compromised.
This build uses MapLibre and Android's built-in location APIs instead of Google Maps and Play Services. Map tiles are fetched from tiles.openfreemap.org, which sees the map area you view (but not your identity or shared locations).

firefox-addons:782160.description:
About This Extension 
The Firefox Multi-Account Containers extension lets you carve out a separate box for each of your online lives – no more opening a different browser just to check your work email!
Under the hood, it separates website storage into tab-specific Containers. Cookies downloaded by one Container are not available to other Containers. You can even integrate individual Containers with Mozilla VPN to protect your browsing and location. With the Firefox Multi-Account Containers extension, you can...
 Sign in to two different accounts on the same site (for example, you could sign in to work email and home email in two different Container tabs.
 Keep different kinds of browsing far away from each other (for example, you might use one Container tab for managing your Checking Account and a different Container tab for searching for new songs by your favorite band)
 Avoid leaving social-network footprints all over the web (for example, you could use a Container tab for signing in to a social network, and use a different tab for visiting online news sites, keeping your social identity separate from tracking scripts on news sites)
 Protect your browsing activity in individual Containers using Mozilla VPN, so you can shop while travelling abroad but check your bank account from a server in your home country.
After installing the Firefox Multi-Account Containers extension, click the Containers icon to edit your Containers. Change their colors, names, and icons. Long-click the new tab button to open a new Container tab.
 For more information on how to use Multi-Account Containers, visit our help articles: 
 All about Multi Account Containers

apple-itunes:568421864.name: Develop! Film Timer
apple-itunes:568421864.description:
Develop your film with a smile!
Develop! is a flexible, elegant timer for developing film and working in the darkroom. Build your own development recipes in a few taps: as many steps as you need, each with its own agitation intervals. It's entirely up to you; you're in full control.
Notable features:
- Voice Control: Hands wet? Just say "NEXT" to move on to the next step. Recognition runs on your iPhone, no internet connection needed.
- Keeps time in the background: Leave the app or lock your phone and the timer keeps running. You'll get a notification when a step ends and at every agitation.
- Intervals: A built-in interval timer handles things like "beep after the first minute, then every 30 seconds." You'll see at a glance how long until your next inversion.
- Darkroom Mode: A strict red-on-black theme for darkroom use.
- Flexible: As many recipes and steps as you like, steps of up to 90 minutes, named your way, with notes for every recipe.
- Easy to read: A large timer you can see across the room, styled after a classic camera body, right down to the vulcanite.
- Import: Bring in recipes straight from FilmDev.org.
- Share: Send a recipe as a file with Mail, Messages, AirDrop or anything else on the share sheet.
No more losing track of time or forgetting to agitate every 30 seconds. Concentrate on being the best photographer and alchemist you can be, and leave the timing to Develop! Now go out there and shoot a roll of film. Good luck!
100% free. Always.

apple-itunes:428475927.description:
GMA News Online, compatible with tablets and smartphones, continues to deliver breaking news in the Philippines and around the world.
The app's regular features include news content from the various sections of GMA News Online: News, Sports, Money, SciTech, Showbiz, and Lifestyle. Get alerts and notifications on your device when a breaking news story is published. It also showcases videos from GMA and GTV. Aside from this, you will also be able to listen to DZBB and Barangay LS radio streaming 24 hours a day.
Experience optimum browsing and get all the information you need at the palm of your hand. The action bar lets you go directly to your preferred section and manage customization settings. Customize your GMA News Online app by choosing your favorite sections and the number of articles that will be displayed.
When an Internet connection is detected, news stories, photos, and videos are automatically updated with the latest content. You can then browse the news at your leisure. For easier reading, you can adjust the font of the text to a size that suits you. A link on each article gives you the option to view it on the GMA News Online mobile site. When browsing offline, the application loads the most recently downloaded news content.
Enjoy smooth scrolling within the articles, and just swipe to move from one section to another or from one story to the next in the same section. You may also share content to Facebook, X, and email from within the GMA News Online app.
To improve your experience, we bring regular updates with bug fixes and optimizations. Thank you for using GMA News Online.
You may also share the news article via Facebook, X, and email.
